contract: Movement across a 64-unit cell boundary resolves pinned routing. Local ownership reports primary plus neighbors; foreign ownership requests a CHECKMAIN sweep. Ready replicas may answer cell ownership without obtaining write authority.

RELEASEMAIN enters TransferOut, prevents new gameplay dispatch and drains in-flight per-client handlers with a three-second deadline and client-close interruption. Presence is withdrawn and state-store mutations are frozen under its mutex. Exact source-format graph captures current core, raw inventory fields and remaining skill timers.

Prepare journals the exact body/digest and source/target process, connection, catalog and authority identities. A prepared claim cannot checkpoint. Exact prepare retries do not extend its five-second expiry.

Accept requires a ready exact target replica and matching unexpired prepared body. One account-serialized transaction changes the primary epoch, persists incoming core, rebinds checkpoint/other replicas and retains the old source as a ready replica. It never reloads stale durable children.

Target hydration derives client item/stat projections through pinned catalogs and restores skill timers. Full typed extra sections are retained; retaining them does not implement their gameplay. Lost COMMIT confirmation can be retried only with the exact body while the target is still loaded.

Loaded promotion publishes role/epoch/state even if the client closed during commit. Teardown waits for pending ownership publication. CONNECT and empty CONREADY activate the new main; retained connections accept confirmation, and the old source demotes after its consumed receipt is confirmed. Handoffs send no duplicate CHARINFO.

Authority epochs prevent same-socket ABA writes after a round trip. Checkpoint revisions are scoped to connection and authority; late checkpoint failures during ownership transition do not close the new tenure. Old source final-save confirmation never writes the target core.

Version-2 checkpoints atomically retain the complete graph, current supported skill durations, digest, core receipt and catalog identities after transfer. Fresh login restores that graph under a new key; same-revision confirmation requires both core and graph hashes. Pure fresh non-transfer characters still use the existing version-1 core-only path.

Source abort saves the exact prepared journal graph and cancels the transfer. Source replacement can recover frozen prepared state, cancel it and release the account. Target replacement recovers committed loaded/ready graph checkpoints. Core drift/missing receipts remain orphaned; no successful save is fabricated.

Authorized physical deletion of a low-level character cascades its checkpoint and transfer receipts. Map runtime cannot directly delete those receipts. Historical items/skill rows are not rewritten by transfer.
World movement reports require the current typed primary peer, finite coordinates and the complete list/EOF before state or queue mutation.
Native verification holds an exclusive lab lock because TLS server identity is shared across databases in the same disposable PostgreSQL instance.
